heading: INT. FLOODED LAW OFFICE BASEMENT - DEPOSITION ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. FLOODED LAW OFFICE BASEMENT - DEPOSITION ROOM - DAY
A windowless concrete room with six inches of water on the floor.
Sandbags line one wall.
A folding table has been set on cinder blocks, and on it a laptop propped on a stack of phone books.
Waders hang from a coat rack.
ATTORNEY SABINE LEFEBVRE-OTIENO, forties, sits in rolled-up trousers and rubber boots, a legal pad on her knee.
Across from her, her client DOUGLAS "DOUG" NAKAGAWA-FITCH, sixty, stares at the water with the stillness of a man who has resigned himself to it.

At the end of the table, COURT REPORTER MARIAH THRUSH, thirties, types with her feet tucked up on the chair rungs, and on the laptop screen, three small windows hold the faces of the opposing counsel and a stern, silver-haired woman in a judge's robe.
She clears her throat.
He does not look up.
The court reporter's keys clatter.
Mr. Nakagawa-Fitch, is it your testimony that the basement did not flood in March?
units.name: OPPOSING COUNSEL

units.text: It's my testimony that I was elsewhere.
units.name: DOUG

units.text: Elsewhere.
units.name: OPPOSING COUNSEL

units.text: In a canoe.
units.name: DOUG

units.text: A pause.
The silver-haired woman on the screen lifts her chin.
Let the record reflect the witness is, at present, in water.
units.name: JUDGE

units.text: Sabine closes her eyes.
Mariah types it down, unblinking.
Doug lifts one boot and lets the water run off it, ring by ring.
